==English==
{{wp}}

===Alternative forms===
* {{alt|en|'ear||pronunciation spelling}}
* {{alt|en|heare||obsolete}}

===Etymology===
{{etymon|en|id=perceive sound|:inh|enm:heren<id:perceive sound>|tree=1}}
{{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂eḱ-|*h₂ew- (perceive)}}
From {{inh|en|enm|har}}, {{m|enm|heoren}}, {{m|enm|her}}, {{m|enm|here}}, {{m|enm|heren}}, from {{inh|en|ang|hēran}}, {{m|ang|hīeran}}, {{m|ang|hīran}}, {{m|ang|hȳran|t=to hear}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*hauʀijan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*hauzijaną|t=to hear}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*h₂ḱh₂owsyéti|t=to be sharp-eared}}, from {{m|ine-pro|*h₂eḱ-|t=sharp}} + {{m|ine-pro|*h₂ows-|t=ear}} + {{m|ine-pro|*-yéti}} (denominative suffix).
{{col-top|2|cog}}
Cognate with {{cog|frr|hear}}, {{m|frr|hiar}}, {{m|frr|hiir}}, {{m|frr|hiire|t=to hear}}, {{cog|stq|heere}}, {{m|stq|here|t=to hear}}, {{cog|fy|hearre|t=to hear}}, {{cog|bar|hearn|t=to hear}}, {{cog|gmw-cfr|hüre|t=to hear}}, {{cog|cim|hòrran}}, {{m|cim|höarn|t=to hear}}, {{cog|nl|horen|t=to hear}}, {{cog|de,nds|hören|t=to hear}}, {{cog|lb|héieren|t=to hear}}, {{cog|yi|הערן|t=to hear}}, {{cog|da,nb|høre|t=to hear}}, {{cog|ovd|ära|t=to hear}}, {{cog|fo|hoyra|t=to hear}}, {{cog|is|heyra|t=to hear}}, {{cog|nn|haur}}, {{m|nn|høra}}, {{m|nn|høre}}, {{m|nn|høyra}}, {{m|nn|høyre|t=to hear}}, {{cog|sv|höra|t=to hear}}, {{cog|got|𐌷𐌰𐌿𐍃𐌾𐌰𐌽|t=to hear}}; also {{cog|el|ακούγω}}, {{m|el|ακούω|t=to hear}}, {{cog|grk-ita|κούω|t=to hear}}, {{cog|txb|āks-|t=to awaken}}.
{{col-bottom}}

===Verb===
{{wikidata lexeme|L184}}
{{en-verb|~s|~ing|~d}}

# {{lb|en|intransitive|stative}} To [[perceive]] sounds through the [[ear]]. {{defdate|from 10th c.}}
#: {{ux|en|I was deaf, but now I can '''hear'''.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|stative}} To [[perceive]] (a sound, or something producing a sound) with the [[ear]], to [[recognize]] (something) in an auditory way. {{defdate|from 10th c.}}
#: {{syn|en|catch}}
#: {{ux|en|I could '''hear''' them quarreling upstairs, but didn’t really listen to their argument.}}
#* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=4|passage=Mr. Cooke at once began a tirade against the residents of Asquith for permitting a sandy and generally disgraceful condition of the roads. So roundly did he vituperate the inn management in particular, and with such a loud flow of words, that I trembled lest he should be '''heard''' on the veranda.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To exercise this faculty [[intentionally]]; to [[listen]] to. {{defdate|from 10th c.}}
#* {{RQ:Tyndale NT|John|X|text=Agayne there was dissencion amonge the iewes for these sayinges, and many of them sayd: He hath the devyll, and is madde: why '''heare''' ye hym?}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To listen favourably to; to [[grant]] (a request etc.). {{defdate|from 10th c.}}
#: {{ux|en|Eventually the king chose to '''hear''' her entreaties.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To receive information about; to come to [[learn]] of. {{defdate|from 10th c.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1667|author=w:John Milton|title=w:Paradise Lost|passage=Adam, soon as he '''heard''' / The fatal Trespass don by Eve, amaz'd, / Astonied stood and Blank {{...}} }}
# To be [[contact]]ed by. {{+obj|en|:from}}
#: {{ux|en|I haven't '''heard''' from you in a while; how have you been?}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|law}} To [[listen]] to (a person, case) in a court of law; to [[try]]. {{defdate|from 12th c.}}
#: {{syn|en|adjudge|rule on|try|Thesaurus:adjudicate}}
#: {{ux|en|Your case will be '''heard''' at the end of the month.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|informal}} To [[sympathize]] with; to understand the feelings or opinion of.
#: {{ux|en|You're tired of all the ads on TV? I '''hear''' ya.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|Greek|_|philosophy}} To [[study]] under.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1656|author={{w|Thomas Stanley (author)|Thomas Stanley}}|title=The History of Philosophy. The Eighth Part, Containing the Stoick Philosophers|page=15|pageurl=https://books.google.co.uk/books?id=CerJrvesOw0C&pg=PA15|text=''SPHÆRUS'' was of ''Bosphorus'', he first '''heard''' ''Zeno'', then ''Cleanthes'', and having made a sufficient progresse in learning, went to ''Alexandria'' to ''Ptolomy Philopater'' {{...}}}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1990|author=Henry J. Blumenthal|chapter=Themistius: the last Peripatetic commentator on Aristotle?|editor=Richard Sorabji|title=Aristotle Transformed: The Ancient Commentators and Their Influence|edition=2nd|year_published=2016|isbn=9781472589071|pages=130–31|pageurl=https://books.google.co.uk/books?id=5aEyEAAAQBAJ&pg=PA130|text=Ammonius, the teacher of both Simplicius and Philoponus, tells us how Julian gave a ruling {{...}} in favor of Maximus, who had '''heard''' Iamblichus, and followed him and Porphyry (''in An. Pr.'' 31,15–22).}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2018|chapter=Introduction: The Old Academy to Cicero|editors=Harold Tarrant; et al.|title=Brill’s Companion to the Reception of Plato in Antiquity|isbn=9789004270695|pages=24–25|pageurl=https://books.google.co.uk/books?id=loRXDwAAQBAJ&pg=PA24|text=Charmadas, never actually Head of School but a prominent Academic who had himself '''heard''' Carneades, was prepared to teach Plato’s ''Gorgias'' {{...}}}}

====Usage notes====
* This is generally a [[stative verb]] that rarely takes the continuous inflection. See [[:Category:English stative verbs]]
